about: Trainchecker 'Your train passes near…'. One item per stretch between neighbouring stations, keyed by the stretch's id (its two station codes in alphabetical order). network holds every station and every stretch with any of it in England, as [a, b, length in metres], from stretches.json (OpenStreetMap, © OpenStreetMap contributors, Open Database Licence). In an item, a and b are the stretch in the direction the research was done; side is the side of the train when travelling from a to b (facing forwards): swap left and right for b to a. text has {side} for 'left' or 'right'; textReverse, where present, replaces text for b to a. England only. Every fact checked against its source.

PNZ-SER.name: Penzance Heliport
PNZ-SER.text: Your train passes near Penzance Heliport, on the train's {side}, where helicopters to the Isles of Scilly started flying again in 2020 after an eight-year gap.

LTS-SER.name: St Erth station
LTS-SER.text: St Erth station, at one end of this stretch, is listed Grade II and is the junction for the St Ives Bay Line.

HYL-SER.name: Harvey & Co foundry, Hayle
HYL-SER.text: Your train passes the old offices of Harvey & Co, on the train's {side}, the foundry John Harvey set up in Hayle in 1779.

CBN-HYL.name: Trevithick Cottage
CBN-HYL.text: Your train passes near Trevithick Cottage, on the train's {side}, childhood home of the Cornish engineer Richard Trevithick, now cared for by the National Trust.

CBN-RED.name: Carn Brea
CBN-RED.text: Your train passes near the hill of Carn Brea, on the train's {side}, with a Neolithic enclosure, a medieval castle and old mine workings on it.

RED-TRU.name: Wheal Busy
RED-TRU.text: Your train passes near Wheal Busy, on the train's {side}, a mine that produced huge amounts of copper in the 18th century, now part of the Cornish mining World Heritage Site.

PRW-TRU.name: Carnon Viaduct
PRW-TRU.text: Your train crosses Carnon Viaduct, 96 feet high, over Restronguet Creek. The first viaduct here had timber on stone piers; a new stone viaduct replaced it in 1933.

PRW-PYN.name: Ponsanooth Viaduct
PRW-PYN.text: Your train crosses Ponsanooth Viaduct over the River Kennal. At 139 feet high, it is the tallest viaduct west of Truro.

PNM-PYN.name: Collegewood Viaduct
PNM-PYN.text: Your train crosses Collegewood Viaduct, 954 feet long. When it was rebuilt in stone in 1934, it was the last timber viaduct in Cornwall to be replaced; the piers of the old one still stand.

FMT-PNM.name: National Maritime Museum Cornwall
FMT-PNM.text: Your train passes near the National Maritime Museum Cornwall, on the train's {side}, in a harbourside building that opened in February 2003. It looks after the National Small Boat Collection, which came from the National Maritime Museum in Greenwich.

FAL-FMT.name: Pendennis Castle
FAL-FMT.text: Your train passes near Pendennis Castle, on the train's {side}, an artillery fort built for Henry VIII between 1540 and 1542. In the Civil War its Royalist garrison held out through a long siege until August 1646.

SAU-TRU.name: Truro Cathedral
SAU-TRU.text: Your train passes near Truro Cathedral, on the train's {side}, built between 1880 and 1910 on the site of St Mary's parish church.

PAR-SAU.name: Charlestown
PAR-SAU.text: Your train passes near Charlestown harbour, on the train's {side}, a port that grew in the late 18th century from the fishing village of West Polmear and has changed little since.

LUX-PAR.name: Treffry Viaduct
LUX-PAR.text: Your train passes beneath the Treffry Viaduct, built of granite by Joseph Treffry between 1839 and 1842 to carry his tramway, and water for his Fowey Consols mine, across the Luxulyan Valley.

BGL-LUX.name: Luxulyan
BGL-LUX.text: Your train passes near Luxulyan, on the train's {side}, which gives its name to luxulyanite, a rare Cornish granite used for the Duke of Wellington's sarcophagus in St Paul's Cathedral.

BGL-ROC.name: Holy well north-west of Roche station
BGL-ROC.text: Your train passes near an old holy well north-west of Roche station, on the train's {side}, protected as a scheduled monument.

ROC-SCR.name: Goss Moor
ROC-SCR.text: Your train crosses Goss Moor, a national nature reserve and the largest continuous mire in south-west Britain. The A30 once ran through the middle of it.

QUI-SCR.name: St Columb Road station
QUI-SCR.text: St Columb Road station, at one end of this stretch, was first called Halloon; it took its present name in 1878. It is a request stop.

NQY-QUI.name: Trenance Viaduct
NQY-QUI.text: Your train crosses Trenance Viaduct, 141 metres long, over the Trenance valley in Newquay. The first, of timber on stone piers, opened in 1849; today's masonry viaduct dates from 1939.

LOS-PAR.name: Duchy Palace, Lostwithiel
LOS-PAR.text: Your train passes near the Duchy Palace in Lostwithiel, on the train's {side}, once the centre from which the Dukes of Cornwall ran their estates.

BOD-LOS.name: Restormel Castle
BOD-LOS.text: Your train passes near Restormel Castle, on the train's {side}, a Norman castle known for its perfectly circular design.

BOD-LSK.name: Moorswater Viaduct
BOD-LSK.text: Your train crosses Moorswater Viaduct. Beside it stand the stone piers of the earlier viaduct, which carried the line on timber, as Brunel advised for Cornwall's valleys.

COE-LSK.name: Liskeard Viaduct
COE-LSK.text: Your train passes beneath Liskeard Viaduct, 150 feet high, which carries the main line. The Looe branch has run under it since 1901.

COE-SKN.name: Coombe Junction Halt
COE-SKN.text: At Coombe Junction Halt, at one end of this stretch, trains between Liskeard and Looe change direction: the driver and guard swap ends.

CAU-SKN.name: St Keyne Wishing Well Halt
CAU-SKN.text: St Keyne Wishing Well Halt, at one end of this stretch, shares its name with St Keyne's holy well. In Victorian times it was said that whichever of a newly married couple drank from it first would have the upper hand.

CAU-SDP.name: Liskeard and Looe Union Canal
CAU-SDP.text: Your train runs along the valley of the East Looe River, beside the remains of the Liskeard and Looe Union Canal. It was finished in 1828 with 24 locks, and fell out of use after the railway was built in 1860.

LOO-SDP.name: Old Guildhall, Looe
LOO-SDP.text: Your train passes near the Old Guildhall in East Looe, on the train's {side}, believed to date from around 1450.

LSK-MEN.name: St Martin's Church, Liskeard
LSK-MEN.text: Your train passes near St Martin's Church, Liskeard, on the train's {side}, the second-largest parish church in Cornwall.

MEN-SGM.name: St Germans Priory
MEN-SGM.text: Your train passes near St Germans church, on the train's {side}, once the seat of the Saxon bishops of Cornwall.

SGM-STS.name: Trematon Castle
SGM-STS.text: Your train passes near Trematon Castle, on the train's {side}, a Norman motte-and-bailey castle with a 12th-century keep, overlooking the River Lynher.

LEL-LTS.name: Lelant Saltings
LEL-LTS.text: Your train runs beside Lelant Saltings, on the train's {side}, part of the Hayle Estuary, where the RSPB manages a nature reserve.

CBB-LEL.name: St Uny's Church, Lelant
CBB-LEL.text: Your train passes Lelant's parish church of St Uny, on the train's {side}, listed Grade I, with Norman work in its nave arcades.

CBB-SIV.name: Barbara Hepworth Museum
CBB-SIV.text: Your train passes near Trewyn Studio, on the train's {side}, which the sculptor Barbara Hepworth bought in 1949. She lived and worked there until her death in 1975; it is now a museum and sculpture garden.

CSK-GSL.name: Morwellham Quay
CSK-GSL.text: Your train passes near Morwellham Quay, on the train's {side} across the Tamar in Devon, a river port that grew up to serve the local mines. It is now an open-air museum.

BAS-CSK.name: Calstock Viaduct
BAS-CSK.text: Your train crosses the Tamar between Devon and Cornwall on Calstock Viaduct, 120 feet high, with 12 arches built from 11,148 concrete blocks between 1904 and 1907.

BAS-BFE.name: St Andrew's Church, Bere Ferrers
BAS-BFE.text: Your train passes near St Andrew's Church in Bere Ferrers, on the train's {side}, whose stained glass is the oldest in Devon outside Exeter Cathedral.

BFE-SBV.name: Tavy Bridge
BFE-SBV.text: Your train crosses the mouth of the River Tavy, just before it joins the Tamar, on the Tavy Bridge, 453 metres long.

SBF-SBV.name: St Budeaux connection
SBF-SBV.text: Your train uses a link between the two railways at St Budeaux, put in on March 21st 1941 so that trains could get round bomb damage. Since 1964, when the old line into Devonport closed, all trains from Victoria Road have used it.

KEY-SBF.name: HMS Drake
KEY-SBF.text: Your train passes near HMS Drake, on the train's {side}: not a ship but a "stone frigate", the naval barracks for Devonport.

DOC-KEY.name: HMNB Devonport
DOC-KEY.text: Your train passes near Devonport naval base, on the train's {side}, the largest naval base in Western Europe.

DOC-DPT.name: Devonport Park
DOC-DPT.text: Your train passes near Devonport Park, on the train's {side}, laid out in the 1850s on former military land.

DPT-PLY.name: Mount Pleasant Redoubt
DPT-PLY.text: Your train passes near Mount Pleasant Redoubt, on the train's {side}, an earthwork fort built around 1780 to guard the dockyard against a French and Spanish invasion.

IVY-PLY.name: Saltram House
IVY-PLY.text: Your train passes near Saltram House, on the train's {side}, which Nikolaus Pevsner called "the most impressive country house in Devon", with interiors by Robert Adam.

IVY-TOT.name: Totnes Castle
IVY-TOT.text: Your train passes near Totnes Castle, on the train's {side}, one of the best-preserved Norman motte-and-bailey castles in England.

NTA-TOT.name: Forde House, Newton Abbot
NTA-TOT.text: Your train passes near Forde House, on the train's {side}, a manor house of about 1550, enlarged around 1610 and known for its 17th-century carving and plasterwork.

NTA-TGM.name: Shaldon
NTA-TGM.text: Your train runs beside the Teign estuary, with the village of Shaldon across the water on the train's {side}.

NTA-TRR.name: Forde House
NTA-TRR.text: Your train passes near Forde House, on the train's {side}, enlarged around 1610. Charles I stayed there in 1625, and William of Orange in 1688, a few days after landing at Brixham.

TQY-TRR.name: Torre Abbey
TQY-TRR.text: Your train passes near Torre Abbey, on the train's {side}, founded in 1196 for Premonstratensian canons and now the best-preserved medieval monastery in Devon and Cornwall.

PGN-TQY.name: Oldway Mansion
PGN-TQY.text: Your train passes near Oldway Mansion, on the train's {side}, built for the sewing-machine maker Isaac Singer and rebuilt by his son Paris in the style of the Palace of Versailles.

DWL-TGM.name: Parson and Clerk
DWL-TGM.text: As your train goes through Parson's Tunnel, the two rock stacks it is named after, the Parson and Clerk, stand just off the headland on the train's {side}.

DWL-DWW.name: Langstone Rock
DWL-DWW.text: Your train passes Langstone Rock, on the train's {side}, a red sandstone headland that the sea, and then Brunel's railway, cut off from the mainland.

DWW-SCS.name: Starcross Pumping House
DWW-SCS.text: Your train passes Brunel's pumping house at Starcross, on the train's {side}, built in 1845 for his atmospheric railway, whose trains ran for less than a year. It is the only complete pumping house left from the three atmospheric lines in the British Isles.

MBT-SCS.name: Powderham Castle
MBT-SCS.text: Your train passes near Powderham Castle, on the train's {side}, a fortified manor house on the bank of the Exe estuary, listed Grade I.

EXT-MBT.name: Custom House, Exeter
EXT-MBT.text: Your train passes near Exeter's Custom House, on the train's {side}, built in the late 17th century, the first in England built for the purpose.

EXD-EXT.name: Exeter Cathedral
EXD-EXT.text: Your train passes near Exeter Cathedral, on the train's {side}, complete by about 1400, with the longest unbroken medieval stone-vaulted ceiling in the world.

EXD-NTC.name: Cowley Bridge
EXD-NTC.text: Your train passes near Cowley Bridge, on the train's {side}, a three-arched classical bridge built in 1813 and 1814 by James Green, surveyor to the county of Devon.

CDI-NTC.name: Church of St Cyriac and St Julitta, Newton St Cyres
CDI-NTC.text: Your train passes near the parish church of Newton St Cyres, on the train's {side}, built in the 15th century of a reddish local volcanic stone. Inside is a standing effigy of John Northcote, who died in 1632.

CDI-YEO.name: Church of the Holy Cross, Crediton
CDI-YEO.text: Your train passes near Crediton's Church of the Holy Cross, on the train's {side}, on the site of the cathedral of the bishops of Crediton until the see moved to Exeter in 1050.

OKI-YEO.name: Roman forts at North Tawton
OKI-YEO.text: Your train passes near the site of Roman forts at North Tawton, on the train's {side}, where the Romans crossed the River Taw. The fort is thought to have been called Nemetostatio.

OKE-OKI.name: Okehampton Castle
OKE-OKI.text: Your train passes near Okehampton Castle, on the train's {side}, built between 1068 and 1086 after a revolt in Devon against Norman rule. It is now a ruin.

COP-YEO.name: Copplestone Cross
COP-YEO.text: Your train passes Copplestone Cross, on the train's {side}, an ancient carved granite pillar listed Grade I, standing where three old parishes meet.

COP-MRD.name: Church of St Mary the Virgin, Down St Mary
COP-MRD.text: Your train passes near the church of St Mary the Virgin at Down St Mary, on the train's {side}, listed Grade I and rebuilt in the 1400s. One of the two old crosses in its churchyard was found being used as a paving slab in Bow, and put back up between 1897 and 1909.

LAP-MRD.name: Roman fort at Bury Barton
LAP-MRD.text: Your train passes near the site of a Roman fort at Bury Barton, on the train's {side}, thought to be a large early fort that was followed by a smaller one.

EGG-LAP.name: Church of St Thomas of Canterbury, Lapford
EGG-LAP.text: Your train passes near Lapford's church of St Thomas of Canterbury, on the train's {side}, listed Grade I. Inside is a late 15th-century screen, carved on both sides.

EGG-KGN.name: Gatehouse at Colleton
EGG-KGN.text: Your train passes near the gatehouse at Colleton, on the train's {side}, probably from the 1400s and listed Grade I. Its upper floor was once a chapel, licensed in 1402.

KGN-PMA.name: Kings Nympton station
KGN-PMA.text: Kings Nympton station, at one end of this stretch, opened in 1854 as South Molton Road. It was renamed in 1951 to avoid confusion with South Molton station on the line to Taunton.

PMA-UMB.name: Brightley Barton
PMA-UMB.text: Your train passes near Brightley Barton, on the train's {side}, on a hillside above the River Taw. From the early 1500s to 1715 it was the seat of the Giffard family, and the medieval stone walls of their house's moat still survive, a great rarity in North Devon.

CPN-UMB.name: Umberleigh House and Holy Trinity Chapel
CPN-UMB.text: Your train passes near Umberleigh House, on the train's {side}, a Georgian farmhouse listed Grade I with the ruins of the medieval chapel of the Holy Trinity beside it. The Devon historian Tristram Risdon wrote that the site was once a palace of the Saxon king Æthelstan.

BNP-CPN.name: Barnstaple Long Bridge
BNP-CPN.text: Your train passes near Barnstaple's Long Bridge over the River Taw, on the train's {side}, one of the largest medieval bridges in Britain. A will of 1274 left money for its upkeep.

EXC-EXD.name: Rougemont Castle
EXC-EXD.text: Your train passes near Rougemont Castle, on the train's {side}, built into a corner of Exeter's Roman walls from 1068, after the city rebelled against William the Conqueror. In 1682 the three Devon Witches, the last people in England executed for witchcraft, were tried there.

EXD-TVP.name: St Andrew's Church, Cullompton
EXD-TVP.text: Your train passes near St Andrew's Church, Cullompton, on the train's {side}, mostly 15th-century and known for its fan-vaulted Lane Aisle.

TAU-TVP.name: Tonedale Mills, Wellington
TAU-TVP.text: Your train passes near Tonedale Mills in Wellington, on the train's {side}, the largest textile mill in South West England, famous for Taunton serge and later the khaki cloth and puttees of the British Army.

BWT-TAU.name: Taunton Castle
BWT-TAU.text: Your train passes near Taunton Castle, on the train's {side}, now the Museum of Somerset. In its Great Hall in 1685 Judge Jeffreys held the Bloody Assizes after the Monmouth Rebellion, and 144 men were hanged.

CLC-TAU.name: Athelney
CLC-TAU.text: Your train passes near Athelney, on the train's {side}, where Alfred the Great hid before defeating the Vikings at Edington in 878, and where he later founded an abbey.

CLC-YVP.name: Haynes Motor Museum
CLC-YVP.text: Your train passes near the Haynes Motor Museum at Sparkford, on the train's {side}, with more than 300 cars and motorcycles. It was founded in 1985 by John Haynes, of the Haynes workshop manuals, in a disused sawmill.

THO-YVP.name: Newton Surmaville
THO-YVP.text: Your train passes near Newton Surmaville, on the train's {side}, a house built between 1608 and 1612 for the clothier Robert Harbin and listed Grade I.

THO-YET.name: Upbury Farm, Yetminster
THO-YET.text: Your train passes near Upbury Farm in Yetminster, on the train's {side}, where a blue plaque remembers the farmer Benjamin Jesty, born in the village. In 1774, some 20 years before Edward Jenner's vaccine, he used cowpox to give immunity against smallpox.

CNO-YET.name: St Andrew's Church, Yetminster
CNO-YET.text: Your train passes near St Andrew's Church in Yetminster, on the train's {side}, listed Grade I and mostly from the mid-1400s. Its faceless clock, some 300 years old, chimes the national anthem every three hours.

CNO-MDN.name: Church of St Peter and St Paul, Cattistock
CNO-MDN.text: Your train passes near the church at Cattistock, on the train's {side}, rebuilt in the 1800s by Sir George Gilbert Scott and his son. The son's tall tower earned it the name "Cathedral of the Frome Valley".

DCW-MDN.name: Poundbury Camp
DCW-MDN.text: Your train runs in a tunnel beneath Poundbury Camp, an Iron Age hillfort above Dorchester. Brunel wanted a cutting through it, but local outrage meant the more expensive tunnel was built instead.

DCW-UPW.name: Maumbury Rings
DCW-UPW.text: Your train passes near Maumbury Rings, on the train's {side}, a Neolithic henge that the Romans made into an amphitheatre and the Civil War into an artillery fort. In 1846 the route planned for the Southampton and Dorchester Railway was changed to spare it.

DCH-UPW.name: Ridgeway Hill Viking burial pit
DCH-UPW.text: Your train passes near Ridgeway Hill, on the train's {side}, where in June 2009 archaeologists found a pit holding the remains of 54 Scandinavian men, executed some time between 970 and 1025. They are thought to have been Vikings killed by the local Anglo-Saxons.

UPW-WEY.name: King's Statue, Weymouth
UPW-WEY.text: Your train passes near the King's Statue in Weymouth, on the train's {side}, put up in 1809 for George III's Golden Jubilee. The king came to Weymouth on holiday 14 times, the first in 1789.

BRU-CLC.name: Bruton Dovecote
BRU-CLC.text: Your train passes near the Bruton Dovecote, on the train's {side}, a stone tower built between the 15th and 17th centuries that may have been a lookout before it housed pigeons.

BRU-FRO.name: Marston Moat
BRU-FRO.text: Your train passes near Marston Moat, on the train's {side}, the moat of a fortified manor house held by the Bigot family before 1195. There is some evidence they fortified it without the king's licence; that, and an insult to the king's messenger, cost Richard Bigot his lands.

FRO-WSB.name: Berkley House
FRO-WSB.text: Your train passes near Berkley House, on the train's {side}, home of Squire Thomas Prowse, who built the church of St Mary beside it in 1751. The church has a glazed cupola over its nave.

TRO-WSB.name: Handle House, Studley Mills
TRO-WSB.text: Your train passes near the Handle House at Studley Mills in Trowbridge, on the train's {side}, which straddles the River Biss. It was used to dry and store teasels, which were used to raise the nap of cloth.

BOA-TRO.name: Bradford-on-Avon Tithe Barn
BOA-TRO.text: Your train passes near the tithe barn at Barton Farm, on the train's {side}, built in the 1330s for the nuns of Shaftesbury Abbey, the richest nunnery in England. It is listed Grade I and looked after by English Heritage.

AVF-BOA.name: St Laurence's Church, Bradford-on-Avon
AVF-BOA.text: Your train passes near St Laurence's Church in Bradford-on-Avon, on the train's {side}, one of very few Anglo-Saxon churches in England without later medieval changes. For many years it was used as a school and a cottage, until William Jones, rector of the parish church of Holy Trinity, rediscovered it in 1856.

AVF-FFD.name: Avoncliff Aqueduct
AVF-FFD.text: Your train passes under Avoncliff Aqueduct, next to Avoncliff station, which carries the Kennet and Avon Canal over the River Avon and the railway. It was built by John Rennie and John Thomas between 1797 and 1801.

BTH-FFD.name: Claverton Pumping Station
BTH-FFD.text: Your train passes near Claverton Pumping Station, on the train's {side}, built by John Rennie between 1809 and 1813. The River Avon turns its great water wheel, which pumps water 48 feet up to the Kennet and Avon Canal, on the other side of the railway.

BTH-OLF.name: Roman Baths
BTH-OLF.text: Your train passes near the Roman Baths, on the train's {side}, where the Romans built a temple at the hot spring between AD 60 and 70.

KYN-OLF.name: Saltford Brass Mill
KYN-OLF.text: Your train passes near Saltford Brass Mill, on the train's {side}, the last survivor of more than 30 mills that once worked along this stretch of the Avon.

BTH-CPM.name: Central Government War Headquarters, Corsham
BTH-CPM.text: While your train is in Box Tunnel, the government's secret Cold War headquarters, built in an old stone quarry, lies just to the train's {side}.

CPM-MKM.name: Yelde Hall, Chippenham
CPM-MKM.text: Your train passes near the Yelde Hall in Chippenham's Market Place, on the train's {side}, built in about 1450 and once the meeting place of Chippenham Borough Council. It is listed Grade I.

MKM-TRO.name: Staverton Mill
MKM-TRO.text: Your train passes near Staverton Mill, on the train's {side}, a mill on the River Avon since the Domesday Book. Once a woollen mill and later a Nestlé milk factory, it makes breakfast cereals: Shredded Wheat and Shreddies moved there in 2007.

CPM-SWI.name: STEAM, Museum of the Great Western Railway
CPM-SWI.text: Your train passes near STEAM, the Museum of the Great Western Railway, on the train's {side}. It is in a workshop of Swindon Works, built around 1842 with stone from Box Tunnel.

BPW-SWI.name: Health Hydro, Swindon
BPW-SWI.text: Your train passes near the Health Hydro in Swindon, on the train's {side}, built for the Great Western Railway's Medical Fund Society. Its Turkish baths carry on a service begun for railway workers and their families in 1868, the longest-surviving Victorian Turkish baths in the world; in 1948 the fund's medical services became part of the new NHS.

BPW-FIT.name: Stoke Gifford depot
BPW-FIT.text: Your train passes near Stoke Gifford depot, on the train's {side}, built on a triangle of land between three railway lines. It was built to look after Great Western Railway's Class 800 trains, which entered service in 2017.

ASD-FIT.name: New Orphan Houses, Ashley Down
ASD-FIT.text: Your train passes near the New Orphan Houses on Ashley Down, on the train's {side}, built between 1849 and 1870 by George Müller. Their five houses held 2,050 children at a time, and Müller never asked anyone for money to run them.

ASD-SRD.name: St Werburgh's Church, Bristol
ASD-SRD.text: Your train passes near St Werburgh's Church, on the train's {side}, a medieval church that stood in Corn Street in the old city until 1879, when it was taken down and rebuilt here. Its 14th-century tower was moved stone by stone; the church is now a climbing centre.

MTP-SRD.name: St Paul's Church, Bristol
MTP-SRD.text: Your train passes near St Paul's Church in Portland Square, on the train's {side}, begun in 1789 and listed Grade I. It closed in 1988 and is now Circomedia, a circus school.

MTP-RDA.name: Redland Chapel
MTP-RDA.text: Your train passes near Redland Chapel, on the train's {side}, built in 1742 as a private chapel for John Cossins of Redland Court and listed Grade I. Now the parish church, it is unusual in having no patron saint.

CFN-RDA.name: Clifton Lido
CFN-RDA.text: Your train passes near the Lido in Clifton, on the train's {side}, opened as the Clifton Victoria Baths in 1850. It closed in 1990 and was considered for demolition, but was restored and reopened in 2008.

CFN-SML.name: Abona Roman town
CFN-SML.text: Your train runs through the site of Abona, a small Roman port town at the mouth of the River Trym. Much Roman material was dug up when the dock at Sea Mills was built.

SHH-SML.name: Kings Weston House
SHH-SML.text: Your train passes near Kings Weston House, on the train's {side}, built between 1712 and 1719 to designs by Sir John Vanbrugh for the lawyer and politician Edward Southwell.

PRI-SHH.name: Avonmouth Bridge
PRI-SHH.text: Your train passes near the Avonmouth Bridge, on the train's {side}, which carries the M5 over the River Avon. It is 4,554 feet long, with a main span of 538 feet.

AVN-PRI.name: Pill Lifeboat Station
AVN-PRI.text: Your train passes near Pill, across the river on the train's {side}, where the RNLI kept a lifeboat for little more than three years, from July 1971 to November 1974.

AVN-SAR.name: Avonmouth Docks
AVN-SAR.text: Your train passes near Avonmouth Docks, on the train's {side}, part of the Port of Bristol where the Avon meets the Severn estuary. Today they are one of the UK's main ports for chilled foods, especially fruit and vegetables.

SAR-SVB.name: Lawrence Weston Wind Turbine
SAR-SVB.text: Your train passes near the Lawrence Weston wind turbine, on the train's {side}, owned by the community it helps to fund. When it started turning in May 2023 it was the tallest onshore wind turbine in England, 150 metres to the tip of its blades.

LWH-SRD.name: Northern Storm Water Interceptor
LWH-SRD.text: Your train passes near Bristol's Northern Storm Water Interceptor, on the train's {side}: a tunnel about 16 feet across that carries floodwater from the River Frome at Eastville three miles under the city to the Avon Gorge. It was finished in 1962.

BRI-LWH.name: Brunel's Old Station, Temple Meads
BRI-LWH.text: Your train passes near Brunel's original Temple Meads station, on the train's {side}, opened on August 31st 1840 as the western end of the Great Western Railway. It is listed Grade I and no longer used by trains.

BMT-BRI.name: St Mary Redcliffe
BMT-BRI.text: Your train passes near St Mary Redcliffe, on the train's {side}, whose spire is 274 feet high. Elizabeth I is said to have called it "the fairest, goodliest and most famous parish church in England" on a visit in 1574.

BMT-PSN.name: St John the Baptist's Church, Bedminster
BMT-PSN.text: Your train passes near the site of St John the Baptist's Church in Bedminster, on the train's {side}, one of Bristol's oldest churches, first recorded in 1003. It was gutted in the Blitz in November 1940 and in 1967 the council approved the demolition of its ruins.

NLS-PSN.name: Tyntesfield
NLS-PSN.text: Your train passes near the park of Tyntesfield, on the train's {side}, around a Victorian Gothic house remodelled in the 1860s for William Gibbs, whose fortune came from guano. The National Trust bought it in 2002.

NLS-YAT.name: Strawberries and Cream Tree
NLS-YAT.text: Your train passes near the Strawberries and Cream Tree in Backwell, on the train's {side}, a cherry tree with white blossom on one side and pink on the other: a wild cherry grafted with a Japanese one. Children in Backwell gave it its name.

WOR-YAT.name: St Mary's Church, Yatton
WOR-YAT.text: Your train passes near St Mary's Church in Yatton, on the train's {side}, built around 1400. It is often called the Cathedral of the Moors, as it is so large for the village.

HIG-WOR.name: The Helicopter Museum
HIG-WOR.text: Your train passes near the Helicopter Museum, on the train's {side}, with more than 80 helicopters and autogyros from around the world. It began as the private collection of the aviation writer Elfan ap Rees and opened to the public in 1978.

BWT-HIG.name: Castle Street, Bridgwater
BWT-HIG.text: Your train passes near Castle Street in Bridgwater, on the train's {side}, built in the 1720s for the Duke of Chandos on the site of Bridgwater Castle. Many of its houses are listed Grade I.

HIG-WSM.name: Tropicana (Dismaland)
HIG-WSM.text: Your train passes near the Tropicana, a disused lido in Weston-super-Mare, on the train's {side}, where Banksy secretly built Dismaland, his "bemusement park", in 2015. It was open for 36 days and had 150,000 visitors.

WNM-WSM.name: Grand Pier, Weston-super-Mare
WNM-WSM.text: Your train passes near Weston-super-Mare's Grand Pier, on the train's {side}, opened in 1904. Its pavilion has burned down twice, in 1930 and in 2008.

WNM-WOR.name: Worle Town station (site)
WNM-WOR.text: Your train passes near the site of Worle Town station, on the train's {side}, on the Weston, Clevedon and Portishead Railway. It opened in 1897 and closed in May 1940; with no gates at its level crossing, it saw several accidents.

FIT-PWY.name: Stoke Gifford depot
FIT-PWY.text: Your train passes Stoke Gifford depot, on the train's {side}, opened in 2016 on a triangle of land between three railway lines. It looks after Great Western Railway's Class 800 trains.

PIL-PWY.name: The Wave
PIL-PWY.text: Your train passes near The Wave, on the train's {side}, an artificial lake for surfing that opened in 2019, with wave machines from the Spanish company Wavegarden.

CDT-PIL.name: Severn Tunnel
CDT-PIL.text: Your train runs through the Severn Tunnel under the estuary of the River Severn, opened in 1886. It is 7,008 metres long, and until 1987 it was the longest underwater tunnel in the world.

BPW-PWY.name: Gipsy Patch Lane Bridge
BPW-PWY.text: Your train crosses Gipsy Patch Lane on a bridge built in 2020. It replaced a narrow dark-brick arch, so that the road could have a bus lane each way.

BPW-YAE.name: Huckford Viaduct
BPW-YAE.text: Your train crosses the Huckford Viaduct, built by the Great Western Railway in 1902 about 100 feet above the River Frome, which runs through one of its arches.

CDU-YAE.name: Holy Trinity Church, Wickwar
CDU-YAE.text: Your train passes near Holy Trinity, Wickwar's parish church, on the train's {side}. It stands on a small hill, reached by a raised path called the Stank, meaning "dam": there were fish ponds here until the 1800s.

CDU-GCR.name: Frocester Court barn
CDU-GCR.text: Your train passes near the barn at Frocester Court, on the train's {side}, a late 13th-century estate barn listed Grade I. The remains of a Roman villa have been found in the grounds.

CDU-CNM.name: Stonehouse Court
CDU-CNM.text: Your train passes near Stonehouse Court, on the train's {side}, a manor house of 1601 that is now a hotel. An earlier owner of the manor, John Maltravers, was found guilty of a part in the murder of Edward II in 1327.

CNM-SHU.name: Dean Close School
CNM-SHU.text: Your train passes near Dean Close School, on the train's {side}, opened in 1886. Its grounds, some 50 acres, are the largest single private area of land in Cheltenham.

GCR-SHU.name: Siege of Gloucester
GCR-SHU.text: Your train passes near the centre of Gloucester, on the train's {side}, which held out against Charles I's army for nearly four weeks in 1643, until a Parliamentarian army under the Earl of Essex arrived and the siege was lifted.

SHU-STD.name: Stanley Mills
SHU-STD.text: Your train passes near Stanley Mills, on the train's {side}, a woollen mill built in 1813 to be fireproof, with cast-iron columns holding up brick vaults. Five waterwheels on the River Frome once drove it, and its main building is listed Grade I.

KEM-STD.name: Sapperton Canal Tunnel
KEM-STD.text: Your train passes near one end of the Sapperton Canal Tunnel, on the train's {side}. When it opened in 1789 it was the longest tunnel of any kind in England, and it kept the title until 1811. Boats were legged through it until 1911.

KEM-SWI.name: Swindon Mechanics' Institute
KEM-SWI.text: Your train passes near the Mechanics' Institute in Swindon, on the train's {side}, founded in 1843 to give evening classes and a library to the Great Western Railway's workers. Its building of 1854 and 1855 has stood empty since the works closed in 1986.

DID-SWI.name: Uffington
DID-SWI.text: Your train passes near the village of Uffington, on the train's {side}, where Thomas Hughes, author of Tom Brown's School Days, was born in 1822. The poet John Betjeman lived there from 1934 to 1945.

APF-DID.name: Didcot Railway Centre
APF-DID.text: Your train passes Didcot Railway Centre, on the train's {side}, a railway museum in what was once a Great Western Railway engine shed.

APF-CUM.name: Appleford Railway Bridge
APF-CUM.text: Your train crosses the Thames on Appleford Railway Bridge. The first bridge here, of timber, was finished in 1844; today's steel one dates from 1927.

CUM-RAD.name: Culham fusion research site
CUM-RAD.text: Your train passes near the Culham fusion research site, on the train's {side}. Its Joint European Torus began work in 1983 and in 1991 became the first reactor in the world to run on the deuterium and tritium fuel meant for future power stations.

OXF-RAD.name: St Mary the Virgin, Iffley
OXF-RAD.text: Your train passes near St Mary the Virgin, Iffley, on the train's {side}, built in the second half of the 12th century and one of the best-preserved Norman churches in England.

HND-OXF.name: St Barnabas Church, Oxford
HND-OXF.text: Your train passes near St Barnabas Church in Jericho, Oxford, on the train's {side}, built like an Italian basilica with a bell tower. It appears in Thomas Hardy's Jude the Obscure, and John Betjeman wrote a poem about it.

CME-HND.name: Blenheim Palace
CME-HND.text: Your train passes near the park of Blenheim Palace, on the train's {side}, built between 1705 and 1722 and now a World Heritage Site. Winston Churchill was born there.

CME-FIN.name: North Leigh Roman Villa
CME-FIN.text: Your train passes near North Leigh Roman Villa, on the train's {side}, which grew from the late first century into a very large, luxurious house with 19 mosaic floors. It is in the care of English Heritage.

CBY-FIN.name: Cornbury Park
CBY-FIN.text: Your train runs along the edge of Cornbury Park, on the train's {side}, once a royal hunting estate: Domesday Book calls it a "demesne forest of the king". It still holds a remnant of the Wychwood Forest.

AUW-CBY.name: Ascot d'Oilly Castle
AUW-CBY.text: Your train passes near the mound of Ascot d'Oilly Castle, on the train's {side}, named after Roger d'Oilly, who was given the land by William the Conqueror. His brother built Oxford Castle.

AUW-SIP.name: Ascott Earl Castle
AUW-SIP.text: Your train passes near the mound of Ascott Earl Castle, on the train's {side}, a motte-and-bailey castle built on Iron Age earthworks. A second castle, Ascot d'Oilly, stands at the other end of the village.

KGM-SIP.name: Bruern Abbey
KGM-SIP.text: Your train passes near Bruern Abbey, on the train's {side}, where Nicholas Basset founded a Cistercian abbey in 1147. The country house there now was built in 1720.

KGM-MIM.name: Adlestrop (former station)
KGM-MIM.text: Your train passes the site of Adlestrop station, closed in 1966. On June 24th 1914 the poet Edward Thomas's express made a stop here, and he wrote the poem "Adlestrop" about it; a station sign and a bench are now in the village bus shelter.

HYB-MIM.name: Roman town at Dorn
HYB-MIM.text: Your train runs past the site of a small Roman town at Dorn, the largest of five defended towns on the Fosse Way between Cirencester and Lincoln. Here the line reaches its highest point between Oxford and Worcester.

EVE-HYB.name: Battle of Evesham
EVE-HYB.text: Your train passes the battlefield of Evesham, on the train's {side}, where on August 4th 1265 the future Edward I defeated Simon de Montfort, who was killed in the fighting.

EVE-PSH.name: Evesham Abbey bell tower
EVE-PSH.text: Your train passes near the bell tower of Evesham Abbey, on the train's {side}, built in the 1500s. Almost all of the abbey was pulled down at the Dissolution, but the tower still stands.

PSH-WOP.name: Mucknell Abbey
PSH-WOP.text: Your train passes near Mucknell Abbey, on the train's {side}, an Anglican Benedictine monastery of monks and nuns on what was a farm. The community moved here from Burford Priory.

WOP-WOS.name: The Commandery
WOP-WOS.text: Your train passes near the Commandery in Worcester, on the train's {side}, the Royalist army's headquarters at the Battle of Worcester on September 3rd 1651. It is listed Grade I and open to visitors.

WOF-WOS.name: Worcester Cathedral
WOF-WOS.text: Your train passes near Worcester Cathedral, on the train's {side}, founded in 680. King John, who died in 1216, is buried there.

MVL-WOF.name: Worcester Racecourse
MVL-WOF.text: Your train passes near Worcester Racecourse, known locally as Pitchcroft, on the train's {side}, beside the River Severn. Horses have raced there since at least 1718.

GMV-MVL.name: Great Malvern Priory
GMV-MVL.text: Your train passes near Great Malvern Priory, on the train's {side}, a Benedictine monastery from about 1075 and now the parish church. It has the largest display of 15th-century stained glass in England.

CWL-GMV.name: Colwall Tunnel
CWL-GMV.text: Your train runs through the Colwall Tunnel under the Malvern Hills. The first tunnel here opened in 1861; it was replaced on August 2nd 1926 by the wider one in use today.

CWL-LED.name: Ledbury Tunnel
CWL-LED.text: Your train runs through Ledbury Tunnel, bored through the limestone of Dog Hill and opened in 1861. It has never been widened, and carries a single track for its whole length of 1,323 yards.

HFD-LED.name: Hereford Cathedral
HFD-LED.text: Your train passes near Hereford Cathedral, on the train's {side}, home of the Mappa Mundi, a map of the world made around 1300, and of the largest library of chained books in the world.

ASC-WOP.name: Bredon Barn
ASC-WOP.text: Your train passes near Bredon Barn, on the train's {side}, a 14th-century barn built for the Bishops of Worcester. The National Trust has had it since 1951; it was badly damaged by fire in 1979 and restored by 1983.

ASC-CNM.name: Christ Church, Cheltenham
ASC-CNM.text: Your train passes near Christ Church in Cheltenham, on the train's {side}, a Gothic Revival church begun in 1837 and consecrated in 1840. Inside hangs a glass cross engraved by the artist Bryant Fedden.

CNM-GCR.name: Greyfriars, Gloucester
CNM-GCR.text: Your train passes near the remains of Greyfriars in Gloucester, on the train's {side}, a friary founded about 1231. Around 1518 the Berkeleys of Berkeley Castle paid for its church to be rebuilt.

CHO-DID.name: St Mary's Church, Cholsey
CHO-DID.text: Your train passes near St Mary's Church, Cholsey, on the train's {side}, where Agatha Christie is buried.

CHO-GOR.name: Moulsford Railway Bridge
CHO-GOR.text: Your train crosses the Thames on Moulsford Railway Bridge, known locally as Four Arches. Brunel set its brick arches at a slant across the river.

GOR-PAN.name: Basildon Park
GOR-PAN.text: Your train passes near Basildon Park, on the train's {side}, an 18th-century house that played Netherfield, Mr Bingley's home, in the 2005 film of Pride & Prejudice.

PAN-TLH.name: Mapledurham Watermill
PAN-TLH.text: Your train passes near Mapledurham Watermill, on the train's {side} across the Thames, the last working watermill on the river.

RDW-TLH.name: Reading Festival bridge
RDW-TLH.text: Your train passes near the place where the Reading Festival bridge crosses the Thames, on the train's {side}: a temporary footbridge first built in 2008 and put up each year for festival-goers only.

RDW-THE.name: Garston Lock
RDW-THE.text: Your train passes near Garston Lock, on the train's {side}, one of only two working turf-sided locks left on the Kennet and Avon Canal. Its sloping grass sides use more water than brick ones.

AMT-THE.name: Folly Farm, Sulhamstead
AMT-THE.text: Your train passes near Folly Farm, on the train's {side}, a house that Edwin Lutyens extended around 1906 and 1912, with gardens he designed with Gertrude Jekyll.

AMT-MDG.name: Aldermaston Lock
AMT-MDG.text: Your train passes near Aldermaston Lock, on the train's {side}, built between 1718 and 1723 and later given unusual scalloped brick walls.

MDG-THA.name: Midgham Lock
MDG-THA.text: Your train passes near Midgham Lock, on the train's {side}, one of the locks built between 1718 and 1723 under the engineer John Hore of Newbury, when the River Kennet was made navigable.

NRC-THA.name: Monkey Marsh Lock
NRC-THA.text: Your train passes near Monkey Marsh Lock, on the train's {side}, a turf-sided lock from the 1720s that is now a scheduled monument.

NBY-NRC.name: West Berkshire Museum
NBY-NRC.text: Your train passes near the West Berkshire Museum, on the train's {side}, partly housed in Newbury's Cloth Hall, built in 1627 as a cloth factory.

KIT-NBY.name: Litten Chapel
KIT-NBY.text: Your train passes near the Litten Chapel, on the train's {side}, an early 16th-century chapel of Newbury's medieval St Bartholomew's hospital, with finely carved timber roof trusses.

HGD-KIT.name: Church of St Mark and St Luke, Avington
HGD-KIT.text: Your train passes near the church of St Mark and St Luke at Avington, on the train's {side}, an unspoilt Norman church listed Grade I.

BDW-HGD.name: Somerset Hospital, Froxfield
BDW-HGD.text: Your train passes near the Somerset Hospital at Froxfield, on the train's {side}: almshouses for widows left by Sarah, Duchess of Somerset, the oldest part built in 1694.

BDW-PEW.name: Crofton Pumping Station
BDW-PEW.text: Your train passes Crofton Pumping Station, on the train's {side}. Its Boulton & Watt steam engine of 1812 is the oldest working beam engine in the world still in its original engine house.

PEW-WSB.name: Edington Priory
PEW-WSB.text: Your train passes near Edington Priory church, on the train's {side}, built by William Edington, Bishop of Winchester, and consecrated in 1361.

DMH-WSB.name: Dilton Marsh station
DMH-WSB.text: Your train passes Dilton Marsh station, opened as a halt in 1937 with no staff. A sign sent passengers to the seventh house up the hill, where Mrs H. Roberts sold tickets from her home until 1947.

DMH-WMN.name: St Mary's Church, Old Dilton
DMH-WMN.text: Your train passes near St Mary's Church at Old Dilton, on the train's {side}, built in the 14th century beside the Biss Brook and listed Grade I. It is now cared for by the Churches Conservation Trust.

SAL-WMN.name: Wilton House
SAL-WMN.text: Your train passes near Wilton House, on the train's {side}, home of the Earls of Pembroke for more than 400 years. It stands on the site of Wilton Abbey, which Henry VIII gave to William Herbert after the Dissolution.

DEN-SAL.name: Salisbury Cathedral
DEN-SAL.text: Your train passes near Salisbury Cathedral, on the train's {side}, built in just 38 years from 1220. Its spire is the tallest in England, and it holds one of the four surviving original copies of Magna Carta.

DBG-DEN.name: West Dean
DBG-DEN.text: Your train passes near West Dean, on the train's {side}, a village with the border between Wiltshire and Hampshire running through it. A Roman villa site here lies across the border too.

DBG-ROM.name: Romsey Abbey
DBG-ROM.text: Your train passes near Romsey Abbey, on the train's {side}, the church of a Benedictine nunnery until the Dissolution and now the largest parish church in Hampshire. Earl Mountbatten of Burma is buried there.

RDB-ROM.name: Broadlands
RDB-ROM.text: Your train passes near Broadlands, on the train's {side}, the country house that was home to Lord Palmerston, the 19th-century prime minister. In 1767 Capability Brown began remaking the house and its garden.

MBK-RDB.name: King George V Graving Dock
MBK-RDB.text: Your train passes near the King George V Graving Dock in Southampton, on the train's {side}, opened by King George V and Queen Mary in 1933. It was then the largest dry dock in the world, and stayed so for nearly 30 years.

RDW-RGP.name: Elm Park (stadium site)
RDW-RGP.text: Your train passes near the site of Elm Park, on the train's {side}, home of Reading Football Club from 1896 to 1998.

MOR-RGP.name: Reading Green Park station
MOR-RGP.text: Your train passes Reading Green Park station, which opened on May 27th 2023, later than planned because of the Covid-19 pandemic. It serves Reading Football Club's stadium and the Green Park business area.

BMY-MOR.name: Mortimer station
BMY-MOR.text: Mortimer station, at one end of this stretch, keeps its Brunel-designed Great Western Railway buildings, still in use.

BMY-BSK.name: Holy Ghost Chapel ruins, Basingstoke
BMY-BSK.text: Your train passes near the ruins of the Holy Ghost Chapel, on the train's {side}: a chapel stood here by 1244, and Lord Sandys added a family chapel in 1524.

RDG-RDW.name: Greyfriars Church, Reading
RDG-RDW.text: Your train passes near Greyfriars Church, on the train's {side}, the oldest Franciscan church in the UK still used for worship.

RDG-TWY.name: Reading Abbey
RDG-TWY.text: Your train passes near the ruins of Reading Abbey, on the train's {side}, founded by Henry I in 1121. He was buried there in 1136.

EAR-RDG.name: Siege of Reading
EAR-RDG.text: Your train passes near the centre of Reading, on the train's {side}, which a Parliamentarian army of 19,000 under the Earl of Essex besieged for 11 days in April 1643, until the Royalist garrison gave up the town.

EAR-WTI.name: Sol Joel Park
EAR-WTI.text: Your train passes near Sol Joel Park in Earley, on the train's {side}, given to Reading in 1927 by Solomon Joel and opened by the Duke of York, later King George VI.

WNS-WTI.name: Winnersh Film Studios
WNS-WTI.text: Your train passes near Winnersh Film Studios, on the train's {side}, one of the new film studios built in the early 2020s as demand for space to make films and television grew.

WKM-WNS.name: Wokingham Town Hall
WKM-WNS.text: Your train passes near Wokingham Town Hall, on the train's {side}, built in 1860 in the Market Place on the site of an earlier guildhall.

CRN-WKM.name: Lucas Hospital
CRN-WKM.text: Your train passes near the Lucas Hospital, on the train's {side}, almshouses founded in 1663 for 16 elderly men from the parishes around, and listed Grade I.

CRN-SND.name: Wellington College
CRN-SND.text: Your train passes near Wellington College, on the train's {side}, built as a national monument to the first Duke of Wellington. Queen Victoria laid its foundation stone in 1856 and opened it in 1859.

BAW-SND.name: The Concrete Elephant
BAW-SND.text: Your train passes near the Concrete Elephant, on the train's {side}, a sculpture by Barbara Jones made for the Lord Mayor's Show in London in 1963, to show off a builder's use of reinforced concrete. It now stands beside the A30 in Camberley.

BAW-FNN.name: St Michael's Abbey, Farnborough
BAW-FNN.text: Your train passes near St Michael's Abbey in Farnborough, on the train's {side}, founded by the exiled Empress Eugénie as a memorial to her family. She is buried there beside her husband, Napoleon III, and their son.

FNN-NCM.name: Farnborough Hill
FNN-NCM.text: Your train passes near Farnborough Hill, on the train's {side}, a house built for the publisher Thomas Longman and bought in 1880 by the exiled Empress Eugénie of France. It is now a girls' school.

ASH-NCM.name: St Peter's Church, Ash
ASH-NCM.text: Your train passes near St Peter's Church in Ash, on the train's {side}, which dates back to the 12th century. Domesday Book records a church here, probably built of wood.

ASH-WAN.name: Wanborough Roman temple
ASH-WAN.text: Your train passes near the site of a Romano-Celtic temple at Wanborough, on the train's {side}. It was looted between 1983 and 1985; more than a thousand of its silver coins are now in the British Museum.

GLD-WAN.name: University of Surrey
GLD-WAN.text: Your train passes near the University of Surrey, on the train's {side}, which began as the Battersea Polytechnic Institute in London in 1891 and became a university in 1966.

GLD-SFR.name: Guildford Castle
GLD-SFR.text: Your train passes near Guildford Castle, on the train's {side}, built soon after the Norman Conquest of 1066. Its keep still stands.

CHL-SFR.name: Shalford Mill
CHL-SFR.text: Your train passes near Shalford Mill, on the train's {side}, an 18th-century watermill on the River Tillingbourne. In 1932 it was given to the National Trust thanks to Ferguson's Gang, a group of young women who used made-up names.

CHL-GOM.name: Chilworth gunpowder mills
CHL-GOM.text: Your train passes near the ruins of the Chilworth gunpowder mills, on the train's {side}, set up by the East India Company in 1625 beside the Tillingbourne. They supplied gunpowder to the government and closed in 1920.

DKT-GOM.name: Denbies
DKT-GOM.text: Your train passes near Denbies, on the train's {side}, an estate bought in 1734 by Jonathan Tyers of Vauxhall Gardens. Much of its south-facing land is now planted with the vines of Denbies Wine Estate.

DKT-DPD.name: Dorking Cockerel
DKT-DPD.text: Your train passes near the Dorking Cockerel, on the train's {side}, a large sculpture of 2007 on the Deepdene roundabout. It shows a Dorking chicken, a local breed, complete with the breed's fifth toe.

BTO-DPD.name: Betchworth Castle
BTO-DPD.text: Your train passes near the ruins of Betchworth Castle, on the train's {side}, a medieval fortified manor house on a sandstone spur above the River Mole.

BTO-REI.name: Reigate Priory
BTO-REI.text: Your train passes near Reigate Priory, on the train's {side}, founded in the 1200s as an Augustinian priory. After the Dissolution it became a house; one later owner was Charles Howard, who led the English fleet against the Spanish Armada.

RDH-REI.name: Reigate Castle
RDH-REI.text: Your train passes near the site of Reigate Castle, on the train's {side}, now a public park. None of the castle buildings survive, but a cave below it, Baron's Cave, is sometimes open for tours.

ELD-RDH.name: Royal Earlswood Hospital
ELD-RDH.text: Your train passes near the Royal Earlswood Hospital, on the train's {side}, the first establishment to care specifically for people with learning disabilities. John Langdon Down, after whom Down's syndrome is named, ran it from 1855 to 1868.

TWY-WGV.name: Loddon Nature Reserve
TWY-WGV.text: Your train passes near Loddon Nature Reserve, on the train's {side}, 14 hectares run by the Berks, Bucks and Oxon Wildlife Trust.

SHI-WGV.name: Hannen Columbarium, Wargrave
SHI-WGV.text: Your train passes near St Mary's churchyard in Wargrave, on the train's {side}, where the Hannen family's columbarium, a resting place for ashes, was designed by Edwin Lutyens.

HOT-SHI.name: Henley Bridge
HOT-SHI.text: Your train passes near Henley Bridge, on the train's {side}, built in 1786 with five stone arches across the Thames.

MAI-TWY.name: Church of St James, Ruscombe
MAI-TWY.text: Your train passes near the Church of St James, Ruscombe, on the train's {side}. Its flint chancel dates from the 12th century; the nave and tower were rebuilt in brick in 1638 and 1639.

FZP-MAI.name: All Saints' Church, Boyne Hill
FZP-MAI.text: Your train passes near All Saints' Church at Boyne Hill in Maidenhead, on the train's {side}, completed in 1857 and one of the finest early works of the architect G. E. Street. It is listed Grade I.

COO-FZP.name: Cannoncourt Farm Pit
COO-FZP.text: Your train passes near Cannoncourt Farm Pit, on the train's {side}, old gravel pits where Stone Age tools were found in the early 1900s, among them the largest hand axe ever found.

BNE-COO.name: Bourne End Railway Bridge
BNE-COO.text: Your train crosses the River Thames at Bourne End, on a bridge first built in wood by Isambard Kingdom Brunel for the line's opening in 1854 and rebuilt in steel in 1895.

BNE-MLW.name: Marlow Bridge
BNE-MLW.text: Your train passes near Marlow Bridge, on the train's {side}, a suspension bridge over the Thames built between 1829 and 1832 by William Tierney Clark, who also designed the Chain Bridge over the Danube in Budapest.

MAI-TAP.name: Maidenhead Railway Bridge
MAI-TAP.text: Your train crosses the Thames on Brunel's Maidenhead Railway Bridge, whose two main brick arches are thought to be the longest and flattest ever built. Turner painted a train crossing it in Rain, Steam and Speed (1844).

BNM-TAP.name: Burnham Abbey
BNM-TAP.text: Your train passes near Burnham Abbey, on the train's {side}, founded in 1266 by Richard, Earl of Cornwall, brother of King Henry III. Anglican nuns made it their home from 1916.

BNM-SLO.name: Site of William Herschel's house
BNM-SLO.text: Your train passes near the site of William Herschel's house, on the train's {side}, where he and his sister Caroline built his 40-foot telescope, the largest in the world for 50 years. With it he found two of Saturn's moons in 1789.

SLO-WNC.name: Windsor Castle
SLO-WNC.text: Your train passes near Windsor Castle, on the train's {side}, used by the monarch since the time of Henry I, who reigned from 1100 to 1135: the longest-occupied palace in Europe.

LNY-SLO.name: Kedermister Library, St Mary's Church, Langley
LNY-SLO.text: Your train passes near St Mary's Church, Langley, on the train's {side}. Inside is the Kedermister Library, a parish library from the 1600s still kept in the painted cupboards made for it in 1620.

IVR-LNY.name: Buckinghamshire and Berkshire
IVR-LNY.text: Between Iver and Langley, your train passes from Buckinghamshire into Berkshire.
IVR-LNY.textReverse: Between Langley and Iver, your train passes from Berkshire into Buckinghamshire.

IVR-WDT.name: River Colne
IVR-WDT.text: Your train crosses the River Colne, and about here passes between Greater London and Buckinghamshire.

HAY-WDT.name: Old Vinyl Factory
HAY-WDT.text: Your train passes near the Old Vinyl Factory, on the train's {side}: EMI's old record works, which pressed vinyl records from 1952 until the 1970s.

EXC-SJP.name: Exeter Cathedral
EXC-SJP.text: Your train passes near Exeter Cathedral, on the train's {side}, complete by about 1400. It has the longest unbroken medieval stone vaulted ceiling in the world.

POL-SJP.name: Polsloe Priory
POL-SJP.text: Your train passes near what remains of Polsloe Priory, on the train's {side}, a Benedictine nunnery founded around 1159. At the time it was the only religious house for women in Devon.

DIG-POL.name: Met Office
DIG-POL.text: Your train passes near the headquarters of the Met Office, on the train's {side}. The national weather service moved here from Bracknell in 2003; it was founded in 1854 as a service to sailors.

DIG-NCO.name: Sandy Park
DIG-NCO.text: Your train passes near Sandy Park, on the train's {side}, home of the Exeter Chiefs rugby club since 2006, beside junction 30 of the M5.

NCO-TOP.name: Broadway House, Topsham
NCO-TOP.text: Your train passes near Broadway House in Topsham, on the train's {side}, a red-brick Georgian house of 1776. In the 1800s a naval officer who lived there opened it to the public as a museum of antiquities and fossils.

EXN-TOP.name: Bridge Inn, Topsham
EXN-TOP.text: Your train passes near the Bridge Inn at Topsham, on the train's {side}, a pub since at least 1797 on a site recorded in the Domesday Book. In 1998 Queen Elizabeth II paid what was reported as her first official visit to a pub there.

EXN-LYC.name: Commando Training Centre Royal Marines
EXN-LYC.text: Your train passes the Commando Training Centre Royal Marines, on the train's {side}, the main training centre of the Royal Marines. Lympstone Commando station, opened in 1976, is there to serve it.

LYC-LYM.name: Nutwell Court
LYC-LYM.text: Your train passes near Nutwell Court, on the train's {side}, a neo-classical house of about 1800 on the bank of the Exe estuary, almost facing Powderham Castle on the far side. It was built for a nephew of the last of the Drake baronets, who had lived in the older house here.

EXM-LYM.name: A la Ronde
EXM-LYM.text: Your train passes near the grounds of A la Ronde, on the train's {side}, a 16-sided house built for two cousins, Jane and Mary Parminter, who came home from a tour of Europe and set up house together in Devon in 1795. It now belongs to the National Trust.

SDN-SOU.name: Bargate
SDN-SOU.text: Your train passes near the Bargate, on the train's {side}, the main gateway through Southampton's medieval town walls, built in about 1180. It was used as a prison from at least 1439.

BTE-SDN.name: Clausentum
BTE-SDN.text: Your train passes near Bitterne Manor, on the train's {side}, the site of the Roman settlement of Clausentum, the forerunner of Southampton. The manor house was built from its stones.

BTE-WLS.name: Woolston Floating Bridge
BTE-WLS.text: Your train passes near where the Woolston Floating Bridge crossed the River Itchen, on the train's {side}: a cable ferry that ran from 1836 until 1977, when the Itchen Bridge opened.

SHO-WLS.name: Jesus Chapel, Peartree Green
SHO-WLS.text: Your train passes near Jesus Chapel on Peartree Green, on the train's {side}, consecrated in 1620. Its service is said to have set the pattern for later Church of England consecrations.

NTL-SHO.name: Netley Abbey
NTL-SHO.text: Your train passes near Netley Abbey, on the train's {side}, founded in 1239 for Cistercian monks, who were known for their kindness to travellers. Its ruins later inspired Romantic poets and artists.

HME-NTL.name: Royal Victoria Hospital chapel
HME-NTL.text: Your train passes near the chapel of the Royal Victoria Hospital, on the train's {side}, a military hospital begun in 1856. Its main building was the longest in the world when finished; all but the chapel and one other building were knocked down in 1966.

BUO-HME.name: The Jolly Sailor, Bursledon
BUO-HME.text: Your train passes near the Jolly Sailor at Bursledon, on the train's {side}, an 18th-century pub on the River Hamble that you can reach by boat. It was built as a vicarage and has been a pub since 1845.

BUO-SNW.name: Grace Dieu
BUO-SNW.text: Your train passes near the wreck of the Grace Dieu in the River Hamble, on the train's {side}: Henry V's flagship, launched in 1418 and twice the size of the Mary Rose. She made only one voyage and burned after being struck by lightning in 1439.

FRM-SNW.name: Titchfield Abbey
FRM-SNW.text: Your train passes near Titchfield Abbey, on the train's {side}, founded in 1222. After the abbey was closed in 1537 it became a mansion, later the home of Henry Wriothesley, a patron of Shakespeare.

FRM-PTC.name: Cams Hall
FRM-PTC.text: Your train passes near Cams Hall, on the train's {side}, a Palladian mansion of about 1770 overlooking Portsmouth Harbour. Listed as derelict in 1989, it was restored in the 1990s.

CSA-PTC.name: Wymering Manor
CSA-PTC.text: Your train passes near Wymering Manor, on the train's {side}, the oldest building in Portsmouth. The manor is first recorded in 1042, when it belonged to King Edward the Confessor.

CSA-HLS.name: Hilsea Lines
CSA-HLS.text: Your train passes through the Hilsea Lines, fortifications of the 1700s and 1800s built to guard the way onto Portsea Island, on which most of Portsmouth stands.

FTN-HLS.name: Fratton Park
FTN-HLS.text: Your train passes near Fratton Park, on the train's {side}, home of Portsmouth Football Club since 1899. Being on Portsea Island, it is the only professional English football ground not on the mainland of Great Britain.

FTN-PMS.name: Portsmouth Guildhall
FTN-PMS.text: Your train passes near Portsmouth Guildhall, on the train's {side}, built in 1890 as the town hall. It was badly damaged by bombing in the Second World War and largely rebuilt in the 1950s.

PMH-PMS.name: HMS Warrior
PMH-PMS.text: Your train passes near HMS Warrior, on the train's {side}. Built in 1859 to 1861, she and her sister ship were the first armour-plated, iron-hulled warships. For more than 50 years she served as an oil jetty.

GFD-SGN.name: Greenford station
GFD-SGN.text: Your train passes Greenford station. It was the first London Underground station with an escalator up to the platforms, and until 2014 it had the last wooden escalator on the Underground.

CBP-SGN.name: St Mary's Perivale
CBP-SGN.text: Your train passes near St Mary's Perivale, on the train's {side}, a church of the 12th or 13th century, once the smallest in Middlesex. Cut off from its parish by the A40, it is now an arts centre.

CBP-DRG.name: Cuckoo Schools
CBP-DRG.text: Your train passes near the old Cuckoo Schools, on the train's {side}, opened in 1857 for children of destitute families from London. A working farm educated and fed them until the school closed in 1933.

AML-EAL.name: Ealing Village
AML-EAL.text: Your train passes near Ealing Village, on the train's {side}: five Art Deco blocks of flats built from 1934 to 1936 to tempt film stars from Ealing Studios. In the end, most of the flats went to film crews.

AML-PAD.name: Kensal Green Cemetery
AML-PAD.text: Your train passes near Kensal Green Cemetery, on the train's {side}, where Isambard Kingdom Brunel, the engineer who built this railway, is buried with his father, Marc.

GTW-HOR.name: Gatwick Racecourse
GTW-HOR.text: Your train passes near the site of Gatwick Racecourse, on the train's {side}, now part of the airport. The course opened in 1891 beside the railway, and during the First World War it held a stand-in for the Grand National.

SBF-STS.name: Royal Albert Bridge
SBF-STS.text: Your train crosses the Tamar from Devon into Cornwall on Brunel's Royal Albert Bridge, its two 455-foot iron spans 100 feet above the water.
SBF-STS.textReverse: Your train crosses the Tamar from Cornwall into Devon on Brunel's Royal Albert Bridge, its two 455-foot iron spans 100 feet above the water.

SBV-STS.name: Tamar Bridge
SBV-STS.text: Your train passes the Tamar Bridge, on the train's {side}, which carries the A38 beside the Royal Albert Bridge. When it opened in 1961 it was the longest suspension bridge in Britain.

PIL-STJ.name: Severn Beach
PIL-STJ.text: Your train passes near Severn Beach, on the train's {side}, farmland until the railway came. In the 1920s it became a seaside resort for Bristol, with an open-air pool called the Blue Lagoon, a boating lake and donkey rides.

BRI-KYN.name: Somerdale
BRI-KYN.text: Your train passes near the old Somerdale chocolate factory, on the train's {side}, built for Fry's from 1924 and closed in 2011. Remains of a Roman settlement were found on the site.

KYN-LWH.name: Brislington House
KYN-LWH.text: Your train passes near Brislington House, on the train's {side}, which opened in 1806 as one of the first purpose-built asylums in England. Its design influenced later asylums and Acts of Parliament.

BRU-PEW.name: Sexey's Hospital
BRU-PEW.text: Your train passes near Sexey's Hospital in Bruton, on the train's {side}, almshouses built in about 1630 from the will of Hugh Sexey, an auditor of the Exchequer to James I. People still live there.

BRU-WSB.name: Witham Priory
BRU-WSB.text: Your train passes the site of Witham Priory, on the train's {side}, founded in 1178 or 1179 as the first Carthusian monastery in England.

FRO-PEW.name: Swanborough Tump
FRO-PEW.text: Your train passes near Swanborough Tump, on the train's {side}, a mound where King Aethelred and his brother, the future Alfred the Great, met in 871 on their way to fight the Danes.

PEW-TRO.name: St James's Church, Trowbridge
PEW-TRO.text: Your train passes near St James's Church in Trowbridge, on the train's {side}, built in the 1400s. The poet George Crabbe, rector from 1814 to 1832, is buried there.

ASC-WOS.name: Croome Court
ASC-WOS.text: Your train passes near the park of Croome Court, on the train's {side}: the first landscape designed by Capability Brown, who also designed the house, for the Earl of Coventry in the 1700s.

APF-SWI.name: Priory Cottages, Steventon
APF-SWI.text: Your train passes near Priory Cottages at Steventon, on the train's {side}, a manor house of the 1300s that was a grange of the Abbey of Bec in Normandy. A group of women philanthropists, Ferguson's Gang, gave it to the National Trust in 1939.

DRG-WEA.name: The Drayton Court
DRG-WEA.text: Your train passes near the Drayton Court, on the train's {side}, opened in 1894 and a hotel until the 1940s. In 1914 Ho Chi Minh, later the leader of Vietnam, worked in its kitchens.

PIN-SJP.name: Exeter underground passages
PIN-SJP.text: Your train passes near Exeter's underground passages, on the train's {side}, built to bring water into the medieval city. The oldest date from the 1200s, and you can take a guided tour.

CBK-PIN.name: Battle of Pinhoe
CBK-PIN.text: Your train passes near Pinhoe, on the train's {side}, where the men of Devon and Somerset fought the Danes in 1001. The Danes broke through and burned the village.

CBK-WHM.name: Cranbrook
CBK-WHM.text: Your train passes Cranbrook, on the train's {side}, a new town built on what was farmland. Its first houses were lived in from 2012.

FNT-WHM.name: Whimple
FNT-WHM.text: Your train passes near Whimple, on the train's {side}, home of Whiteway's cider until 1985. The village is still surrounded by cider apple orchards.

FNT-HON.name: Pomeroy Wood
FNT-HON.text: Your train passes near Pomeroy Wood, on the train's {side}, where a Roman military site, probably a fort or a marching camp, was found when the A30 was improved in the 1990s. Its garrison seems to have included cavalry.

AXM-HON.name: Newenham Abbey
AXM-HON.text: Your train passes through the site of Newenham Abbey, a Cistercian abbey founded in 1247 by Reginald de Mohun, a short way south-west of Axminster.

AXM-CKN.name: Forde Abbey
AXM-CKN.text: Your train passes near Forde Abbey, on the train's {side}, a Cistercian monastery whose last abbot surrendered it to the Crown in 1539; it became a house. The philosopher Jeremy Bentham rented it in 1815.

CKN-YVJ.name: Church of All Saints, Sutton Bingham
CKN-YVJ.text: Your train passes near the Church of All Saints at Sutton Bingham, on the train's {side}, from the 1100s and 1200s. Its wall paintings of the 1300s were whitewashed over at the Reformation.

YVJ-YVP.name: Clifton Maybank House
YVJ-YVP.text: Your train passes near Clifton Maybank House, on the train's {side}, a country house with Tudor work surviving. Part of it was taken away to nearby Montacute House.

SHE-YVJ.name: Sherborne Abbey
SHE-YVJ.text: Your train passes near Sherborne Abbey, on the train's {side}, a Saxon cathedral from 705 to 1075, then a Benedictine abbey church, and a parish church since 1539.

SHE-TMC.name: Sherborne Old Castle
SHE-TMC.text: Your train passes near the ruins of Sherborne Old Castle, on the train's {side}, built in the 1100s as the palace of Roger, Bishop of Salisbury. Walter Raleigh leased it in 1592, and Parliament's army took it after a siege in 1645.

GIL-TMC.name: Templecombe Preceptory
GIL-TMC.text: Your train passes near the site of Templecombe Preceptory, on the train's {side}, founded by the Knights Templar in 1185. A face painted on oak panels in about 1280, found in an outhouse in the village, may come from it.

GIL-TIS.name: Old Wardour Castle
GIL-TIS.text: Your train passes near the park of Wardour Castle, on the train's {side}, with the ruins of Old Wardour Castle, built in the 1390s and left uninhabitable after fighting in the Civil War in 1643 and 1644.

SAL-TIS.name: Place Farm, Tisbury
SAL-TIS.text: Your train passes near Place Farm at Tisbury, on the train's {side}, once a grange of Shaftesbury Abbey. Its medieval barn is said to be the largest in England.

GRT-SAL.name: John Halle's Hall
GRT-SAL.text: Your train passes near John Halle's Hall in Salisbury, on the train's {side}, a merchant's hall of the 1400s that is now the foyer of a cinema.

DEN-GRT.name: Borbach Chantry
DEN-GRT.text: Your train passes near Borbach Chantry at West Dean, on the train's {side}, a chapel built in about 1333. When the church it belonged to was pulled down in 1868, the chapel was kept, and it is all that remains.

CPW-LYD.name: Offa's Dyke
CPW-LYD.text: Your train passes near Offa's Dyke at Sedbury, on the train's {side}, the earthwork that roughly follows the border between England and Wales, named after Offa, king of Mercia from 757 to 796.

GCR-LYD.name: Gloucester Cathedral
GCR-LYD.text: Your train passes near Gloucester Cathedral, on the train's {side}. Edward II was buried there in 1327, and it stood in for Hogwarts in the Harry Potter films.

DCH-MTN.name: Max Gate
DCH-MTN.text: Your train passes near Max Gate, on the train's {side}, the house Thomas Hardy designed for himself. He lived there from 1885 until his death in 1928.

MTN-WOO.name: Woolbridge Manor
MTN-WOO.text: Your train passes near Woolbridge Manor, on the train's {side}, a 17th-century house by the old bridge over the River Frome. Its two wall portraits appear in Hardy's Tess of the d'Urbervilles as Tess's ancestors.

WOO-WRM.name: Bindon Abbey
WOO-WRM.text: Your train passes near the ruins of Bindon Abbey, on the train's {side}, a Cistercian monastery that moved here in 1172 from its first site near Lulworth Cove, keeping its old name.

HOL-WRM.name: St Martin's Church, Wareham
HOL-WRM.text: Your train passes near St Martin's Church in Wareham, on the train's {side}, built in about 1020: the most complete Anglo-Saxon church in Dorset. Inside is a stone effigy of T. E. Lawrence.

HAM-HOL.name: Royal Naval Cordite Factory, Holton Heath
HAM-HOL.text: Your train passes near the site of the Royal Naval Cordite Factory, on the train's {side}, set up in the First World War to make cordite for the Navy. Much of it became a nature reserve in 1981.

HAM-POO.name: Poole Stadium
HAM-POO.text: Your train passes Poole Stadium, on the train's {side}, a speedway track built in the early 1930s to give the town some entertainment during the Great Depression.

PKS-POO.name: Scaplen's Court
PKS-POO.text: Your train passes near Scaplen's Court, on the train's {side}, a merchant's house of the late 1400s built of Purbeck and Bath stone and cobbles from Poole Quay. It is now a museum.

BSM-PKS.name: St Aldhelm's Church, Branksome
BSM-PKS.text: Your train passes near St Aldhelm's Church, on the train's {side}, which began as a Sunday mission to the area's pottery workers in a school room in the 1870s.

BMH-BSM.name: Bourne Valley Viaducts
BMH-BSM.text: Your train crosses one of the two Bourne Valley Viaducts over the River Bourne, built in 1888 and 1893; the other is now disused.

BMH-POK.name: St Clement's Church, Bournemouth
BMH-POK.text: Your train passes St Clement's Church, on the train's {side}, built from 1871 to 1873: the first major church designed by J. D. Sedding, and one of three Grade I listed churches in Bournemouth.

CHR-POK.name: Christchurch Castle
CHR-POK.text: Your train passes near Christchurch Castle, on the train's {side}, a Norman castle by the lowest crossing of the River Avon. The Constable's House beside it, of about 1160, is a rare Norman home.

CHR-HNA.name: Christchurch Priory
CHR-HNA.text: Your train passes near Christchurch Priory, on the train's {side}, one of the longest parish churches in the country and as big as many cathedrals.

HNA-NWM.name: Chewton Glen
HNA-NWM.text: Your train passes near Chewton Glen, on the train's {side}, now a hotel. Captain Frederick Marryat stayed there in the 1840s while writing The Children of the New Forest.

NWM-SWY.name: Sway
NWM-SWY.text: Your train passes Sway, on the train's {side}, which the railway reached in 1888. At the southern edge of the village stands Sway Tower, a concrete folly 66 metres tall built from 1879 to 1885, still the tallest unreinforced concrete structure in the world.

BCU-SWY.name: New Zealand General Hospital, Brockenhurst
BCU-SWY.text: Your train passes near the site of a First World War hospital, on the train's {side}, run by New Zealand's army medical corps. It was set up in Brockenhurst in 1916, in two large hotels taken for the purpose.

BCU-LYT.name: Buckland Rings
BCU-LYT.text: Your train passes near Buckland Rings, on the train's {side}, an Iron Age hill fort whose banks and ditches can still be clearly seen.

BCU-BEU.name: Bishop's Dyke
BCU-BEU.text: Your train crosses Bishop's Dyke, an earthwork round land of the Bishop of Winchester. Legend says King John told the bishop he could have as much land as he could crawl round, and the bishop, who was rather fat, managed a large area.

ANF-BEU.name: Denny Lodge
ANF-BEU.text: Your train passes near Denny Lodge, on the train's {side}, the remote building that names a large New Forest parish with no towns, villages, churches or schools.

ANF-TTN.name: Eling Tide Mill
ANF-TTN.text: Your train passes near Eling Tide Mill, on the train's {side}, one of only two working tide mills left in the United Kingdom.

RDB-TTN.name: Redbridge old bridge
RDB-TTN.text: Your train passes near the old bridge of 1793 at Redbridge, on the train's {side}, at the mouth of the River Test, where merchant ships and Royal Navy ships were built in the 1700s and 1800s.

LYP-LYT.name: Lymington Lifeboat Station
LYP-LYT.text: Your train passes near Lymington Lifeboat Station, on the train's {side}, on the west bank of the Lymington River. The RNLI first stationed an inshore lifeboat here in 1965.

ADV-GRT.name: Army Headquarters
ADV-GRT.text: Your train passes near Marlborough Lines, on the train's {side}, home of Army Headquarters, the staff who support the head of the British Army.

ADV-WCH.name: Andover Museum
ADV-WCH.text: Your train passes near Andover Museum and Museum of the Iron Age, on the train's {side}, in a Georgian town house of the 1750s, with finds from the nearby Danebury hill fort.

OVR-WCH.name: Laverstoke Mill
OVR-WCH.text: Your train passes near Laverstoke Mill, on the train's {side}. From the 1720s the Portals made the paper for Bank of England banknotes here; it is now the Bombay Sapphire gin distillery.

BSK-OVR.name: Milestones Museum
BSK-OVR.text: Your train passes Milestones Museum, on the train's {side}, where streets of Victorian and 1930s Hampshire have been recreated indoors. It opened in 2000.

BSK-MIC.name: Basingstoke and Alton Light Railway
BSK-MIC.text: Your train passes near where the Basingstoke and Alton Light Railway set off, on the train's {side}: opened in 1901, the first English railway built under the Light Railway laws. Its track was taken up in 1917 for use in France.

MIC-WIN.name: Hyde Abbey
MIC-WIN.text: Your train passes near the gateway of Hyde Abbey, on the train's {side}, where Alfred the Great, his wife and his son were reburied in 1110. Their remains were lost after the abbey was pulled down in 1538.

SHW-WIN.name: Great Hall, Winchester Castle
SHW-WIN.text: Your train passes near the Great Hall of Winchester Castle, on the train's {side}, all that stands of the castle William the Conqueror founded in 1067 besides its Westgate. On its wall hangs the Round Table, made in the 13th century and repainted for Henry VIII, whose young face is King Arthur's.

ESL-SHW.name: Shawford Down
ESL-SHW.text: Your train passes near Shawford Down, on the train's {side}, a nature reserve of chalk grassland. Its slopes still show strip lynchets, terraces left from the Middle Ages, when it was ploughed as common land.

CFR-ESL.name: Eastleigh
CFR-ESL.text: Your train passes near the middle of Eastleigh, on the train's {side}, a town that grew up in the 1800s around the London and South Western Railway. A Saxon village called East Leah was recorded here as long ago as 932.

CFR-ROM.name: King John's House, Romsey
CFR-ROM.text: Your train passes near King John's House in Romsey, on the train's {side}, said to have been King John's hunting lodge. It was in fact built in 1256, some 40 years after he died, though some of its beams may come from an older building.

ESL-SOA.name: Southampton Airport
ESL-SOA.text: Your train passes Southampton Airport, on the train's {side}, where the prototype Spitfire made its first flight on March 5th 1936. A two-thirds-size model of it, K5054, stands at the road entrance.

SOA-SWG.name: St Mary's Church, South Stoneham
SOA-SWG.text: Your train passes near St Mary's Church at South Stoneham, on the train's {side}, one of the two medieval churches left in Southampton. Parts of it are Norman, and its chancel arch dates from the 1100s.

SDN-SWG.name: South Stoneham House
SDN-SWG.text: Your train passes near South Stoneham House, on the train's {side}, an early 18th-century manor house thought to be by Nicholas Hawksmoor. What is now the University of Southampton bought it in 1921 for students and added a 17-storey tower in 1964; it has stood empty since 2005.

ESL-HDE.name: Eastleigh Works
ESL-HDE.text: Your train passes Eastleigh Works, on the train's {side}, opened by the London and South Western Railway in 1891 to build carriages and wagons. Locomotive building moved here from Nine Elms in London in 1910.

BOE-HDE.name: Shamblehurst Farmhouse
BOE-HDE.text: Your train passes near Shamblehurst Farmhouse, on the train's {side}, a timber-framed house partly from the 1600s, its upper floor jutting out over the lower. It now goes by the name Strawberry Cottage.

BOE-FRM.name: Funtley Deviation
BOE-FRM.text: Your train passes the old Funtley Deviation, on the train's {side}, a two-mile line opened in 1904 to avoid the unstable Fareham tunnel. It had troubles of its own, and closed in May 1973, when trains went back through the tunnel; it is now a footpath.

BSK-HOK.name: Basing House
BSK-HOK.text: Your train passes near Basing House, on the train's {side}, a Tudor palace built from 1531 for William Paulet, Marquess of Winchester, that once rivalled Hampton Court. Cromwell's troops stormed it in October 1645 after a long siege, and local people were encouraged to carry off its bricks.

HOK-WNF.name: Hook Common and Bartley Heath
HOK-WNF.text: Your train passes near Hook Common and Bartley Heath, on the train's {side}, a Site of Special Scientific Interest with large areas of wet heath, a habitat that rarely survives in the Thames Basin.

FLE-WNF.name: Elvetham Heath nature reserve
FLE-WNF.text: Your train passes near the Elvetham Heath nature reserve, on the train's {side}, where heather and gorse are coming back by themselves. Its wet woodland has bog myrtle, a rare plant.

FLE-FNB.name: Fleet Pond
FLE-FNB.text: Your train passes Fleet Pond, on the train's {side}, a fishery first recorded in 1324. The London and Southampton Railway bought it for £50 in the 1830s because it stood in the way, and built an embankment across its northern end.

BKO-FNB.name: Basingstoke Canal
BKO-FNB.text: Your train runs beside the Basingstoke Canal, on the train's {side}, finished in 1794 to link Basingstoke with the Thames. It never made money, became derelict, and was reopened in 1991 after years of restoration.

AHV-BKO.name: Brookwood American Cemetery
AHV-BKO.text: Your train passes near Brookwood American Cemetery, on the train's {side}, the only American military cemetery of the First World War in the British Isles. Its chapel, opened in 1929, bears the names of 563 missing, most of them lost at sea.

AHT-AHV.name: Aldershot Military Cemetery
AHT-AHV.text: Your train passes near Aldershot Military Cemetery, on the train's {side}, laid out in the 1850s when the Army made Aldershot its permanent training base. Nearly 17,000 service people of nine nations are buried there.
